haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Both return 401 with "Invalid email or password." and both add a failure row. An unknown email also runs a dummy bcrypt check, so timing does not reveal the account.
haiku-low.q2: It gets a 429 page, "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." The password is not checked and no failure row is added.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session is deleted. Login with the correct password deletes the session the incoming sid pointed to, then creates a new one.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random session ID, 32 random bytes as hex. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from when the session was created, even with continuous use. Last-seen refreshes only extend the 30-minute idle window, not the 12-hour limit.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the session row if present, clears the sid cookie, and redirects the user to /login.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session the cookie points to, if any, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. With no session, it does the same.
haiku-low.q8: In the sessions table in Postgres, not in app memory. Both instances query Postgres, so any instance finds the session by its ID.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per wrong attempt. Only rows from the last 10 minutes count. The document does not say how the window boundary is computed.
haiku-low.q10: It checks the row exists, under 30 minutes since last_seen_at, and under 12 hours since created_at. If valid, it writes last_seen_at as now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 page: "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again in a minute." No session is created and the cookie is not changed.
haiku-low.q12: An hourly cleanup timer on either app instance deletes sessions past either timeout, plus old failure and expired lock rows.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get the same 401 login page, "Invalid email or password." Both add a failure row and can trigger a lock. An unknown email also runs a dummy bcrypt check so timing doesn't reveal whether the account exists.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked, so the attempt gets a 429 login page ("Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."). The password is never checked, and no failure row is added.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login the old session row that the incoming sid pointed to is deleted. A new session is created with a new random ID, and the new sid cookie is set.
sonnet.q4: The cookie (`sid`) holds only the random session ID. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts can't read it. The document also says it is Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: The 12-hour limit from created_at applies even with continuous use, so the session stops working 12 hours after it was created. The 30-minute idle limit never triggers, because last_seen_at keeps being refreshed.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if present, clears the sid cookie, and redirects to /login. The user sees the login page.
sonnet.q7: It deletes the session the cookie points to, if any. Then it clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, it does the same: clears the cookie and redirects.
sonnet.q8: Session state is kept in the Postgres `sessions` table. Any instance reads the session row from Postgres using the session ID in the sid cookie. The instances share no memory, so Postgres is the shared store.
sonnet.q9: Failures are kept in Postgres, in the `login_failures` table, one row per wrong attempt. Only rows from the last 10 minutes count. The document does not say how the window is computed (for example, which timestamp column is compared).
sonnet.q10: It compares the time since last_seen_at (must be under 30 minutes) and the time since created_at (must be under 12 hours), and it checks that the row exists. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now.
sonnet.q11: The document doesn't cover a database error at the session-create step specifically. The nearest case is "Database down at login", which returns a 503 page ("Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again in a minute."), with no session created and no cookie changed. That case is for the database being down, and the document doesn't say it covers a failed session write after a correct password.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup job, which runs on a timer on either instance, deletes sessions past either timeout (30-minute idle or 12-hour absolute). Until then, expired rows are refused on read.
